messages:
james: noticed a p95/p99 jump ~2134566960-2134567000, looks correlated to tenant T-42. started digging.
incident-bot: [ALERT] latency_anomaly: service=serving-runtime p95=312ms p99=1.6s (+x3) affected_tenants=[T-42] — investigate: https://redwood.internal/alerts/4521 :rotating_light:
anya: grabbing flamegraph and kernel selection trace now. early signal: a fallback to the large-matrix kernel is happening for many short seq requests.
kevin: noisy tenant suspects? queue depth for shard s11 spiked. can we temporarily throttle T-42 to confirm? :thinking_face:
james: yes queue depth up from 10 -> 180, batching heuristics ended up grouping many shortseq requests into a long-kernel path due to wrong kernel-selector heuristic.
anya: attaching profiler summary (excerpt):
```
# top kernels by time
k_large_matmul: 64%
k_small_opt: 9%
softmax_fused: 12%
copy_kvcache: 10%
# note: avg_seq_len=8, but selector picked k_large_matmul (optimized for >=128)
```
marta: heads-up - product telemetry shows user-facing latency increase on a couple of large customers. need quick mitigation and a short customer note if rollback takes >30m.
kevin: mitigation options: 1) throttle T-42 at router (fast), 2) flip feature flag to force `prefer_smallseq_kernel` (risky but targeted), 3) route short-seq traffic to fallback pool. which do we want now?
james: prefer flag flip scoped to runtime pool r-pool-3 + tenant T-42. sequence selector bug: mismatch between estimated seq_len and actual (estimation uses truncated prompt context). quick fix: force small kernel when avg_token_hint < 32.
anya: patch ready: small json flag toggle. snippet: `{"prefer_smallseq_kernel": {"enabled": true, "scope": "tenant:T-42,pool:r-pool-3"}}`.
kevin: i'll apply router throttle first (5rps) so customer impact is limited while we flip flag. applying throttle now: `curl -X POST https://infra-api/route/throttle -d '{"tenant":"T-42","rate":5}'`.
ops-bot: throttle applied to T-42 on shard s11 (5rps).
james: flipping feature flag in prod canary to 10% of nodes in r-pool-3. command: `redwood ff set prefer_smallseq_kernel true --scope tenant=T-42 --canary 10%`.
anya: canary logs show kernel mix shifting: k_small_opt up from 9% -> 42% on canary nodes, p95 on canary nodes down from 320ms -> 95ms.
kevin: roll canary to 100% in r-pool-3. doing step: `redwood ff canary-roll prefer_smallseq_kernel 100 --pool r-pool-3` now.
incident-bot: [UPDATE] mitigation progress — throttle + kernel-flag applied to r-pool-3. observed global p95 dropped to 120ms, p99 to 420ms.
marta: good. please draft a 1-paragraph customer note for impacted tenants summarizing we identified and mitigated a routing/kernel selection issue.
james: drafting: "We observed elevated inference latency for a subset of requests. Root cause: kernel-selector mis-classified short-sequence workloads causing inefficient kernel paths. We've applied a scoped kernel selection flag and temporary throttling; full mitigation complete and monitoring. Reach out to success@redwood for customer specifics." ok?
marta: LGTM. send to #customer-comms after this thread.
kevin: followups: open ticket to fix selector heuristic (estimation vs actual discrepancy) and add unit test coverage for short seq boundary. ticket #RT-981.
anya: also adding a perf regression alert: if k_small_opt share < 20% for avg_seq_len < 32 trigger an anomaly. will PR rule.
james: postmortem action items: 1) fix selector logic (RT-981), 2) improve batching heuristic to avoid cross-tenant grouping leading to kernel path pollination (RT-982), 3) add canary automation for kernel-FFs (RT-983).
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] incident 4521 — mitigation verified, p95 back to baseline. Incident closed at 2134567598.
kevin: removing throttle from T-42: `curl -X POST https://infra-api/route/throttle -d '{"tenant":"T-42","rate":null}'`.
ops-bot: throttle removed for T-42.
anya: leaving metrics collection running for 2h to ensure no recurrence. will attach flamegraphs to RT-981.
james: thanks all. short retro at 16:10 UTC in #eng-runtime if anyone wants to join. :coffee:
marta: thanks team :heart:
